DOCUMENTATION / VERSION 0.1.0 BETA

Your PC, under control.

This early portable release brings together user preferences, three power profiles, diagnostics and a restore center. Source code is included. It is in development and is not digitally signed.

Install & get started

  1. Download the ZIP archive then extract all of its contents to a folder.
  2. Read LISEZ-MOI.md. You can verify the ZIP's SHA-256 with Get-FileHash and the checksum file.
  3. Open ASTRA TWEAKS.exe. Keep all extracted files, including the localization module and translations, in the same folder.
  4. Click Analyze / Refresh : this step is read-only.
  5. In Optimizations, select the preferences that suit your needs, then choose Review my selection. Confirm after reviewing the exact values.

The target is Windows 11 and Windows 10 build 19045 or later with Windows PowerShell 5.1, WPF and .NET Framework. Compatibility varies with hardware, edition and administrator restrictions. Inaccessible keys are unavailable. Write failures are reported and trigger a rollback attempt.

The launcher does not automatically request elevation. It uses -NoProfile -STA -ExecutionPolicy Bypass for this PowerShell process only, without changing the permanent policy. On a managed PC, follow your organization's rules. The executable has no publisher signature and no certificate has been created.

Power profiles

ASTRA uses powercfg to duplicate the active plan and save its ID. Other settings remain inherited from the original plan. No profile forces the minimum CPU state to 100%.

ProfileCPU on ACEPP on ACCPU on battery
Performance5–100 %255–80 %
Balanced5–100 %505–80 %
Eco5–80 %805–80 %

EPP is an energy preference: lower values favor performance, higher values favor power savings. It is not a percentage gain. Battery EPP remains inherited from the current plan. CPU limits do not measure actual clock frequency. Some platforms and Modern Standby configurations may reject plans or settings; the app reports the failure and attempts to restore the previous plan.

Restore & recovery

Journals are saved in %LOCALAPPDATA%\AstraTweaks. ASTRA saves the original existence, type and value of every modified preference. It writes the journal before each attempt and then verifies the value. Created keys may remain empty after their value is removed.

  1. Open Restore and refresh the history.
  2. Restore the latest available operation. Operations are undone in reverse order.
  3. After a process interruption, incomplete operations block new changes until resolved.
  4. If a value changed outside ASTRA, restoration stops and reports a conflict. Review the journal and your configuration before proceeding.

ASTRA-created profiles are deleted during restoration after reactivating the previous plan. ASTRA reports a conflict if another tool changed the active plan. Permissions may also prevent restoration; the journal remains available. These backups are not Windows restore points or file backups. Keep the journals while ASTRA changes remain active.

Import frametimes

Use a CSV from an external measurement tool containing a FrameTimeMs or MsBetweenPresents column. Each row represents a frame; use strictly positive milliseconds and a decimal point. Limits: 20 MB and at least 100 frames. Separate captures by process and session before importing; ASTRA does not automatically filter different applications.

FrameTimeMs
6.94
7.12
6.88
… at least 100 measurement rows …

Average FPS = 1000 / average frametime. The 1% and 0.1% lows equal 1000 divided by the average of the slowest 1% or 0.1% of frametimes (frame count rounded up). Other tools may use different definitions. Compare the same scene, duration, configuration and game version. A difference between two captures is not enough to attribute an improvement to a setting.

Understand diagnostics

CPU and RAM metrics are snapshots that need refreshing. Displayed memory is OS-visible memory. WMI refresh rate data may be incomplete or outdated: verify it in Display Settings. Defender or firewall status may be unavailable or depend on a third-party antivirus.

Network diagnostics send six ICMP requests to the entered IP, with an 800 ms timeout per request. Jitter is the average absolute difference between successive received replies. Missing replies may indicate ICMP filtering; they do not prove an Internet outage. This test does not measure game server latency or promise improved ping.

Beta limitations

  • No built-in FPS capture, DPC/ISR, CPU/GPU temperatures, GPU load or thermal detection.
  • No Adaptive mode or automatic game launch detection.
  • No overclocking, BIOS changes, universal TCP settings, bulk registry cleaning or service disabling.
  • No startup program is disabled automatically. Links open Windows Settings.
  • Registry readback verifies the write, not its effective adoption by every Windows version. Some preferences only take effect at the next sign-in.
  • Automated validation uses simulated providers. No compatibility certification across a fleet of PCs has been performed.

Privacy

The app includes no account, telemetry or report transmission. ICMP diagnostics contact the selected target when the test starts. Exported JSON files may contain hardware and process information; review them before sharing. The website has no analytics or tracking cookies added by ASTRA. Its host may process technical data required to deliver it.
